hero.headline: Before asking where the ball should go, ask what boundary must change.
hero.support: A doctrine of actionable space, pressure, possession, promotion, and repair for reading soccer as the construction and transport of temporary advantages through an adversarial field.

definition.title: Space matters when it changes what can happen next.
definition.body: Relevant soccer space is not empty geometry. It is shaped by player reachability, orientation, support, pressure, timing, cover, passing lanes, defensive responsibility, and the next state a team can construct from the current one.
definition.rule: Judge an action by the team state it creates or preserves, not by ball movement alone.

fieldLens.title: Read the field as changing reachability.

dimensions.name: Access
dimensions.question: Which players, lanes, and zones are realistically reachable before pressure closes them?

dimensions.name: Support
dimensions.question: If the receiver is pressed, which continuations remain available?

dimensions.name: Pressure
dimensions.question: Which options is the opponent removing, delaying, or making expensive?

dimensions.name: Orientation
dimensions.question: Can the next player receive facing useful space or only recycle under constraint?

dimensions.name: Promotion
dimensions.question: Does the action transport an advantage into a more consequential state?

dimensions.name: Repair
dimensions.question: When structure breaks, which action restores support, access, responsibility, or control?

method.title: Five passes through a team state.

passes.name: 1. Bound the phase
passes.question: Where is the ball, which team has functional control, what immediate pressure exists, and what transition risk is live?

passes.name: 2. Map access and support
passes.question: Which receivers and zones can be reached in time, and what support remains after the pass?

passes.name: 3. Read authored pressure
passes.question: Which options is the opponent trying to remove, and which future action are they attempting to force?

passes.name: 4. Promote the advantage
passes.question: Which action carries space, numerical advantage, orientation, or tempo into a more consequential state without destroying continuation?

passes.name: 5. Repair before collapse
passes.question: If the lane closes or structure fragments, what reset preserves enough control to build again?

workedExample.title: Worked phase: the backward pass that restores the attack.
workedExample.setup: A fullback receives near the touchline while an opponent closes from inside-out. The nearby winger is marked, the forward lane is narrow, and a central midfielder is available behind the ball. A forward pass would look progressive on a pass map but may enter the opponent's trap.
workedExample.naiveRead: Playing backward loses territory and appears less attacking.
boundaryTrace: the touchline removes one side of the receiver's escape space
the presser's angle is attempting to make the forward lane predictable
the marked winger offers nominal proximity but weak continuation
the central reset can reopen the far side and change the opponent's pressure orientation
the backward pass is useful if it restores a larger reachable action set and allows the next line to be broken under better conditions
workedExample.promotionTest: The reset is not automatically good. It earns value only if the team uses the restored structure to regain access, move the opponent, or create a more consequential next state.
workedExample.lesson: Progress is not identical to forward ball motion. A temporary loss of territory can be a repair operation when it reconstructs the support and access needed to promote the possession later.
workedExample.scopeNote: This is a constructed tactical teaching phase, not a claim about a specific match, team, or event dataset.

taggingGrammar.title: A candidate analyst vocabulary.
taggingGrammar.rule: Tags should describe observable team-state changes and remain compatible with established event, tracking, and tactical-analysis vocabularies rather than replacing them by fiat.

validation.title: The doctrine becomes useful only if it survives match evidence.
targets: inter-analyst agreement on boundary and repair tags
ability to distinguish possession maintenance from advantage promotion
agreement between qualitative traces and event/tracking data where available
predictive value of pressure-state descriptions for likely next actions
coaching usefulness compared with established tactical language
validation.claimRule: Illustrative fit to familiar soccer situations is not validation. Comparative analyst, coaching, event-data, or tracking-data evidence is required for performance claims.

built: Analyst vocabulary and tactical tagging concepts
proof.claimBoundary: This is a practitioner doctrine and research on-ramp, not a claim to replace established coaching, performance analysis, or sports science.

claimBoundary.title: Practitioner doctrine, not a substitute for established soccer analysis.
safe: Boundary-First Soccer is a working public tactical and analytical framing.
Its concepts can be tested against video, event data, tracking data, coaching interpretation, and established tactical frameworks.
The doctrine should import existing football-analysis language whenever that language already captures the relevant structure.
notEstablished: that the doctrine improves team performance or player development
that the proposed tags are more reliable than established analysis systems
that pressure or promotion can be inferred robustly without suitable observation
that Boundary First terminology is necessary when conventional soccer concepts are sufficient

closing.title: Move the ball when moving the ball changes the field you can act in.
closing.finalLine: Map access. Read pressure. Preserve support. Promote the advantage. Repair before the structure collapses.
